lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To begin, I need to ask you some questions about your child.

**First question: How old is your child?**

This is important because:
- Children under 16 generally qualify automatically (as long as they're not working full-time)
- Children aged 16-19 may qualify if they're in approved education or training
- Children aged 20 or over are not eligible for Child Benefit

Please tell me your child's age.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Thanks for helping me with this. I have one child - Alex, who is 17 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 17 years old.

Since Alex is 17 (which falls in the 16-19 age range), we need to check if they're in approved education or training, as this is a requirement for Child Benefit eligibility at this age.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Which of the following applies to Alex?**

1. **Currently in approved education or training** - Alex is currently enrolled in and attending education or training courses

2. **Recently left education** - Alex left approved education or training within approximately the last 20 weeks

3. **Neither** - Alex is not in education/training and didn't recently leave

Please let me know which situation applies to Alex.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is currently in education - he's studying for his A-levels at the local sixth form college.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Since Alex is currently studying for his A-levels at sixth form college, that's approved education. Now I need to check that the education level meets the requirements for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! A-levels are definitely approved non-advanced education. Now I need to verify a few more details about Alex's education:

**Please confirm the following:**

1. **Is Alex studying at least 12 hours per week of supervised study?** (This typically includes lessons, tutorials, and supervised coursework - A-level students at sixth form colleges typically meet this requirement)

2. **Is this education NOT funded by an employer or linked to an agreed future job with an employer?** (Standard sixth form college A-levels are not employer-funded)

3. **Is Alex unmarried or in a civil partnership, OR if married/in a civil partnership, are they financially dependent on you?**

These are the standard requirements to ensure the education qualifies for Child Benefit purposes.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Yes, I can confirm all of that:

1. Yes, Alex is at sixth form full-time, so definitely more than 12 hours a week of supervised study.

2. That's right - it's just standard sixth form education, nothing to do with any employer.

3. Alex is not married or in a civil partnership.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Alex's A-level studies at sixth form clearly meet all the education requirements for Child Benefit. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work at all)?**

This is important because even if a young person is in approved education, they won't qualify for Child Benefit if they're working 24 or more hours per week.

Does Alex work less than 24 hours per week, or is Alex not working at all?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all - he's just focused on his studies at the moment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: That's great - Alex is focused on his studies. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in their own right?**

Specifically, I need to confirm that Alex is not receiving:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit
- Tax credits
- Or similar benefits in their own name

Does Alex receive any of these benefits in their own right?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

The rules vary by region:
- **English apprenticeships** (all types) would disqualify Alex from Child Benefit
- **Scottish Modern Apprenticeships** would disqualify Alex
- **Welsh Foundation Apprenticeships** are approved (other Welsh apprenticeships disqualify)

You mentioned Alex is studying A-levels at sixth form college, so I'm assuming this is NOT an apprenticeship - can you confirm Alex is not doing any type of apprenticeship?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's correct - Alex is not doing an apprenticeship. He's just doing regular A-levels at sixth form.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Now we've established that Alex qualifies as an eligible child. The next part of the assessment focuses on you as the claimant.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Do you meet the UK residency requirements?**

You qualify if **ANY** of the following applies to you:

1. **You normally live in the UK** (this is the most common situation)
2. You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
3. You have pre-settled status and meet certain conditions (working, studying, or have sufficient resources)
4. You're a Crown servant living abroad

Do you normally live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Are you responsible for Alex?**

You qualify if **ANY** of the following applies:

1. **You live with Alex** (most common situation)
2. You contribute to Alex's upkeep by paying at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit amount towards their care (food, clothes, pocket money, housing, presents, etc.)
3. You pay maintenance for Alex under a court order or agreement

Which of these applies to your situation with Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

For example:
- Alex's other parent
- Another family member
- A previous guardian or caregiver

Only one person can receive Child Benefit for the same child at the same time. If someone else is claiming, they would need to stop their claim before you could start claiming.

Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Which of the following best describes Alex's current living situation?**

1. **In hospital** - Alex is currently in hospital
2. **In care** - Alex is in local authority care
3. **Fostered** - Alex is being fostered
4. **Normal living** - Alex lives at home with you (as you mentioned earlier)

Based on what you've told me, it sounds like Alex is living normally at home with you. Can you confirm this is the case, and that Alex is not currently in hospital, in care, or fostered?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's correct - Alex just lives at home with me. He's not in hospital, care, or being fostered.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Final question: Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, is the local council paying for or contributing to Alex's living costs or care?

This would be things like the council paying for Alex's housing, food, or general maintenance costs (not including things like standard school funding which doesn't affect Child Benefit).

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent news! Based on all the information you've provided, let me navigate to the final outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
# 🎉 Great News! You ARE Eligible for Child Benefit!

Based on our assessment, **you meet all the eligibility requirements** for Child Benefit for Alex.

## Summary:
✅ **Alex qualifies** as an eligible child because:
- He is 17 years old (within the 16-19 age range)
- He's studying A-levels at sixth form college (approved non-advanced education)
- He's studying full-time (12+ hours per week)
- He's not working 24+ hours per week
- He's not receiving benefits in his own right
- He's not in an apprenticeship

✅ **You qualify** as a claimant because:
- You live in the UK
- You live with and are responsible for Alex
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- The local council isn't paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance

## Next Steps to Claim:

1. **Apply online or by post** using form CH2
2. **Prepare the following documents:**
   - Proof of your identity
   - Proof of Alex's identity
   - Alex's birth certificate or adoption certificate

3. **Important note about High Income:** Be aware that if you or your partner earns over £60,000 per year, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit Charge through your tax return. However, you can still claim Child Benefit and choose not to receive payments if you want to protect your National Insurance credits.

4. **Payments:** Child Benefit is typically paid every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)

## More Information:
You can apply and find more details here: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

Is there anything else you'd like to know about your Child Benefit eligibility or the application process?
